headline: Red Sox stumble against Angels as Patriots look toward recovery
morning_brew: That defeat yesterday at Fenway was a real kick in the teeth, with the offense failing to string anything together against the Angels. Jake Bennett had a rough go on the hill, and watching that early deficit balloon while our bats stayed cold was pure agony. It felt like a night where the team just never found its footing on either side of the ball, leaving me to stare at the wall and wonder why we can't just have one relaxing Tuesday night at the park.

Across town, the Patriots are reeling after a tough loss to the Seahawks in their season opener. The news that A.J. Brown is sidelined is a massive blow that hurts our offensive depth right out of the gate. Watching the team struggle to find a rhythm on the road shows we have plenty of work ahead, and losing a key playmaker for the next few weeks puts the pressure on the rest of the roster to step up, though right now I'm feeling like my neighbor Rick, who thinks the whole thing is a targeted conspiracy by the refs.

There is no baseball at the Fens tonight, which is probably a mercy after that showing. It gives everyone a chance to regroup before the Royals arrive for a series starting Friday night. I will be spending the time between now and first pitch avoiding the headlines and hoping for a fresh start when we take the field again to maintain our position in the wild card race, because I'm not ready to pull the plug on the Duck Boat fund just yet.

news_digest.headline: Source: Patriots' A.J. Brown likely out at least 4 weeks
news_digest.dans_take: This is a gut punch to our offense that we absolutely cannot afford.
